entries.sanskrit:
सप्त-विंशे ततः सम्यग् बहु-साधन-योगतः ।

पुं-प्रकृत्योर् विवेकेन मोक्ष-रीतिर् निरूप्यते ॥

विवेक-ज्ञानेन मोक्षम् उपपादयितुं शुद्धस्यैव पुरुषस्य प्रकृत्य्-अविवेकतः पूर्वोक्तं संसारम् अनुस्मारयति---प्रकृति-स्थोऽपीति त्रिभिः । देह-स्थोऽपि नाज्यते न लिप्यते। गुणैस् तत् कृतैः सुख-दुःखादिभिः । निर्गुणत्वाद् अकर्तृत्वं ततोऽविकारित्वं तस्मात् ॥१॥
word_for_word: through the application of many disciplines
by discrimination between Puruṣa and Prakṛti
the method of liberation is explained
to establish liberation through discriminative knowledge
he recalls the previously described saṃsāra
in three verses beginning “even while situated in Prakṛti”
even while situated in the body
is not affected, is not stained
by the guṇas and what they produce
such as pleasure, pain, and the rest
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration:
sapta-viṃśe tataḥ samyag bahu-sādhana-yogataḥ |

puṃ-prakṛtyor vivekena mokṣa-rītir nirūpyate ||

viveka-jñānena mokṣam upapādayituṃ śuddhasyaiva puruṣasya prakṛty-avivekataḥ pūrvoktaṃ saṃsāram anusmārayati---prakṛti-stho’pīti tribhiḥ | deha-stho’pi nājyate na lipyate| guṇais tat kṛtaiḥ sukha-duḥkhādibhiḥ | nirguṇatvād akartṛtvaṃ tato’vikāritvaṃ tasmāt ||1||
entries.literal_english: In the twenty-seventh chapter the way to liberation is properly explained through the combination of many disciplines, by discriminating between Puruṣa and Prakṛti. To establish liberation through discriminative knowledge, Śrīdhara recalls in three verses the previously described saṃsāra that arises for the intrinsically pure Puruṣa from failure to discriminate Prakṛti, beginning “Even while situated in Prakṛti.” Even while situated in the body, the Puruṣa is not affected or stained by the guṇas and their effects, such as pleasure and pain. Because it is without guṇas, it is not an agent; therefore it is changeless.

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्।
entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: The pinned Śrīdhara block explicitly says “न व्याख्यातम्।”

entries.sanskrit: अनिर्वृतः सन् । प्रासङ्गिकैः प्रकृति-सङ्ग-कृतैः । सद्-असन्-मिश्र-योनिषु देव-तिर्यङ् नरादिषु संसार-पदवीं प्राप्नोति ॥३॥
word_for_word: in births mixed with good and bad
among gods, animals, humans, and others
he reaches the course of saṃsāra
entries.literal_english: Being unfulfilled, through incidental bonds produced by association with Prakṛti, he reaches the course of saṃsāra in births mixed with good and bad, such as among gods, animals, humans, and others.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: ननु तर्ह्य् अवास्तवत्वात् संसृतेः, किं तन् निवृत्ति-प्रयासेन ? तत्राह---अर्थे हीति ॥४॥
word_for_word: why make an effort to end it?
with the words “even when the object …”
entries.literal_english: But if saṃsāra is unreal, why make an effort to end it? Śrīdhara answers with the phrase “even when the object …”
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: यतो विषय-ध्यानम् अर्थ-हेतुः, अतो मनो नियन्तव्यम् इत्य् आह---अत एवेति । असताम् इन्द्रियाणां पथि विषय-मार्गे । तीव्रेन दृढेन । विरक्त्या च तीव्रया ॥५॥
word_for_word: because contemplation of sense objects causes material involvement
therefore the mind must be restrained
thus he says “for this very reason”
on the path of the unsteady senses
on the road of sense objects
and detachment too must be intense
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: yato viṣaya-dhyānam artha-hetuḥ, ato mano niyantavyam ity āha---ata eveti | asatām indriyāṇāṃ pathi viṣaya-mārge | tīvrena dṛḍhena | viraktyā ca tīvrayā ||5||
entries.literal_english: Because contemplation of sense objects causes material involvement, the mind must therefore be restrained. “On the path of the unsteady senses” means on the road of sense objects. “Intense” means firm, and detachment too must be intense.

entries.sanskrit: भक्ति-विरक्त्योस् तीव्रत्वे कारणानि वर्णयन् ज्ञानेन मोक्ष-प्रकारम् आह षड्भिः । यमादिभिर् योग-मार्गैश् चित्तम् अभ्यसन् पुनः पुनर् एकाग्री-कुर्वन्न् आत्मानम् उपलभ्य सर्वानुस्यूतम् अद्वयं परमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यत इति षष्ठेनान्वयः । सत्येन निष्कपटेन । भावेन प्रेम्णा ॥६॥
word_for_word: the causes for the intensity of devotion and detachment
the way of liberation through knowledge
by disciplines of yoga beginning with yama
the nondual Supreme Self pervading all
this is the construction with the sixth [verse]
by truth, that is, without deceit
by feeling, that is, by love
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: bhakti-viraktyos tīvratve kāraṇāni varṇayan jñānena mokṣa-prakāram āha ṣaḍbhiḥ | yamādibhir yoga-mārgaiś cittam abhyasan punaḥ punar ekāgrī-kurvann ātmānam upalabhya sarvānusyūtam advayaṃ paramātmānaṃ pratipadyata iti ṣaṣṭhenānvayaḥ | satyena niṣkapaṭena | bhāvena premṇā ||6||
entries.literal_english: While describing the causes by which devotion and detachment become intense, Śrīdhara explains in six verses the way of liberation through knowledge. By practising the mind through disciplines of yoga beginning with yama, repeatedly making it one-pointed, realizing the Self, and attaining the nondual Supreme Self that pervades all, one follows the construction of the sixth verse. “By truth” means without deceit; “by feeling” means by love.

entries.sanskrit: अप्रसङ्गतः सङ्ग-त्यागेन । बलीयसा ईश्वरेऽर्पितेन ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: “By non-attachment” means by relinquishing association. “By the stronger [means]” means by that which is offered to the Lord.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: विविक्त-शरण एकान्त-वासी ॥८॥
word_for_word: one who takes refuge in solitude, dwelling alone
entries.literal_english: “A solitary refuge” means dwelling alone.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: असद्-आग्रहम् अहं-ममताम् । प्रकृतेः पुरुषस्य च दृष्टं तत्त्वं येन, तेन ज्ञानेन ॥९॥
word_for_word: the truth of Prakṛti and Puruṣa, seen
by the knowledge through which [that truth is seen]
entries.literal_english: “Insistence on the unreal” means the notions “I” and “mine.” “By which” means by the knowledge through which the truth of Prakṛti and Puruṣa is seen.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: निवृत्तानि बुद्ध्य्-अवस्थानानि जाग्रद्-आदीनि यस्य सः । अत एव दूरी-भूतम् अन्य-दर्शनं यस्य । आत्मनाहङ्कारावच्छिन्नेनात्मानं शुद्धम् उपलभ्य । एकस्यैवावच्छेदानवच्छेदाभ्यां करण-कर्मत्वे दृष्टान्तम् आह---चक्षुषा चक्षुर्-अवच्छिन्नेनार्केण गगन-स्थम् अर्कम् इव । एवम् आत्म-दृक् शुद्धम् आत्मानं पश्यन् ॥१०॥
word_for_word: the states of the intellect have ceased
for whom the perception of anything else has become distant
by the self delimited by ego
of one and the same thing, through delimitation and non-delimitation
the status of instrument and object
by the sun delimited in the eye
like the sun situated in the sky
thus the seer of the Self
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: nivṛttāni buddhy-avasthānāni jāgrad-ādīni yasya saḥ | ata eva dūrī-bhūtam anya-darśanaṃ yasya | ātmanāhaṅkārāvacchinnenātmānaṃ śuddham upalabhya | ekasyaivāvacchedānavacchedābhyāṃ karaṇa-karmatve dṛṣṭāntam āha---cakṣuṣā cakṣur-avacchinnenārkeṇa gagana-stham arkam iva | evam ātma-dṛk śuddham ātmānaṃ paśyan ||10||
entries.literal_english: For him, the states of the intellect beginning with waking have ceased, and therefore the perception of anything else has become remote. Through the self delimited by ego, he realizes the pure Self. To illustrate how one thing can be both instrument and object through delimitation and non-delimitation, Śrīdhara gives this example: by the sun delimited in the eye, one sees the sun situated in the sky. Thus the seer of the Self beholds the pure Self.

entries.sanskrit: मुक्त-लिङ्गं निरुपाधिकम् असति मिथ्या-भूतेऽहङ्कारे सद्-आभासं सद्-रूपेणाभासमानं ब्रह्म प्राप्नोति । शुद्ध-जीव-स्वरूपाद् विशेषम् आह---सतः कारणस्य प्रधानस्य बन्धुम् अधिष्ठानम् । असतः कार्यस्य चक्षुर् इव प्रकाशकम् । सर्वेषु कार्य-कारणेष्व् अनुस्यूतम् । अद्वयं परिपूर्णम् ॥११॥
word_for_word: manifesting in the form of being
he explains the distinction from the pure individual self
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: mukta-liṅgaṃ nirupādhikam asati mithyā-bhūte’haṅkāre sad-ābhāsaṃ sad-rūpeṇābhāsamānaṃ brahma prāpnoti | śuddha-jīva-svarūpād viśeṣam āha---sataḥ kāraṇasya pradhānasya bandhum adhiṣṭhānam | asataḥ kāryasya cakṣur iva prakāśakam | sarveṣu kārya-kāraṇeṣv anusyūtam | advayaṃ paripūrṇam ||11||
entries.literal_english: He attains Brahman, free from the liṅga and without limiting adjuncts, appearing as real within the unreal, false ego. Its distinction from the pure nature of the individual self is this: Brahman is the basis—the support of Pradhāna, the existent cause; like an eye, it illuminates the unreal effect; it pervades all effects and causes; it is nondual and complete.

entries.sanskrit:
अहङ्कारोपहितेन शुद्ध-ब्रह्म-प्रतिपत्तिं सदृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । जले स्थित आभासः सूर्य-प्रतिबिम्बो यदा गृहान्तर्वर्ति-भित्तौ स्फुरति तदा गृह-कोण-स्थितैः पुरुषैर् भित्त्य्-आदौ स्थले स्थितेन स्वाभासेन सूर्य-प्रतिबिम्बेन यथा प्रथमं जल-स्थ आभासोऽवदृश्यते लक्ष्यते, गगन-स्थस्य गृह-मध्ये प्रतिबिम्बायोगात् । चार्थे तथा-शब्दः । यथा चेत्य् अर्थः । यथा च जल-स्थेन दिवि स्थितः सूर्यो लक्ष्यते ॥१२॥

एवं भूतेन्द्रिय-मनो-मयैः देहेन्द्रिय-मनोभिर् अवच्छिन्नैः स्वाभासैर् आत्म-प्रतिबिम्बैस् त्रि-वृत् त्रि-गुणोऽहङ्कारः सतो ब्रह्मण आभासो यस्मिंस् तेन रूपेण लक्षितः । अहङ्कार-स्थाभासं विना विषयाभासानुत्पत्तेः । अनेन चाहङ्कारेण सद्-आभास-वता सत्य-दृक् परमार्थ-ज्ञप्ति-रूप आत्मा लक्षित इत्य् अर्थः ॥१३॥
word_for_word: realization of pure Brahman through [the self] conditioned by ego
the appearance, the sun’s reflection, situated in water
when it shines on a wall inside a house
then by people standing in a corner of the house
by the sun’s reflection, with its own appearance, situated on a surface such as a wall
यथा प्रथमं जल-स्थः आभासः अवदृश्यते लक्ष्यते
how the appearance situated in water is first seen and recognized
because the sun situated in the sky cannot be reflected into the middle of the house
the word “tathā” has the sense of “and”
यथा च जल-स्थेन दिवि स्थितः सूर्यः लक्ष्यते
and just as the sun situated in the sky is perceived through the one situated in water
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara gives an example for realizing pure Brahman through the self conditioned by ego, beginning with “as.” When the sun’s reflection situated in water shines on an interior wall of a house, people standing in a corner of the house first see and recognize the reflection on the wall by its own appearance, since the sun situated in the sky cannot be reflected into the middle of the house. The word “tathā” has the sense “and”; it means “and just as.” Just as the sun in the sky is perceived through its reflection in water, so the pure Brahman is indicated through ego.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration:
ahaṅkāropahitena śuddha-brahma-pratipattiṃ sadṛṣṭāntam āha---yatheti | jale sthita ābhāsaḥ sūrya-pratibimbo yadā gṛhāntarvarti-bhittau sphurati tadā gṛha-koṇa-sthitaiḥ puruṣair bhitty-ādau sthale sthitena svābhāsena sūrya-pratibimbena yathā prathamaṃ jala-stha ābhāso’vadṛśyate lakṣyate, gagana-sthasya gṛha-madhye pratibimbāyogāt | cārthe tathā-śabdaḥ | yathā cety arthaḥ | yathā ca jala-sthena divi sthitaḥ sūryo lakṣyate ||12||

evaṃ bhūtendriya-mano-mayaiḥ dehendriya-manobhir avacchinnaiḥ svābhāsair ātma-pratibimbais tri-vṛt tri-guṇo’haṅkāraḥ sato brahmaṇa ābhāso yasmiṃs tena rūpeṇa lakṣitaḥ | ahaṅkāra-sthābhāsaṃ vinā viṣayābhāsānutpatteḥ | anena cāhaṅkāreṇa sad-ābhāsa-vatā satya-dṛk paramārtha-jñapti-rūpa ātmā lakṣita ity arthaḥ ||13||

entries.sanskrit:
इदानीं सुषुप्ति-साक्षित्वेन शुद्धात्म-प्रतिपत्तिम् अनुभवतो दर्शयति त्रिभिः । भूतादिष्व् असत्य् असत्-तुल्येऽव्याकृते निद्रया लीनेषु सत्सु यस् तत्र तदा विनिद्रो निरहङ्क्रियस् तम् आत्मानं प्रतिपद्यत इति तृतीयेनान्वयः ॥१४॥

ननु यदि तदा विनिद्रोऽसाव् अस्ति तर्हि जाग्रत्-स्वप्नयोर् इव स्फुटः किं नावभासते तत्राह---पूर्वं स द्रष्टातो द्रष्टृत्वेन स-विकल्पतया स्फुटं प्रतीतः । सुषुप्तौ तु भूतादेर् अहङ्कार-विषयस्य लीनत्वात् तद् विषयेऽहङ्कारे नष्टे सति स्वयम् अनष्टोऽपि मृषैवात्मानं नष्टवन् मन्यमानो यः । अन्यस्य नाशेऽन्यस्य नष्ट-तुल्यत्वे दृष्टान्तः, नष्ट-वित्तो यथा आतुरो विवशः, नष्टवद् भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥

ननु सुषुप्तौ न किञ्चिद् अनुभूयते, मैवम्, "सुखम् अहम् अस्वाप्सं न किञ्चिद् अवेदिषम्" इति विशेष-ज्ञानं विना केवलस्यात्मनः प्रतिसन्धानाद् इत्य् आह---एवम् इति । ननु प्रतिसन्धाने साहङ्कारस्य प्रतीतेः कथं निरहङ्क्रियत्वं तत्राह---साहङ्कारस्य द्रव्यस्य कार्य-कारण-सङ्घातस्यानुग्रहः प्रकाशकः अवस्थानं च । द्रव्य-विशेषणतयाहङ्कारस्यापि दृश्यत्वाच् च तद् द्रष्टात्मा तद् व्यतिरिक्तः । तम् आत्मानम् इत्य् अन्वयः ॥१६॥
word_for_word: as the witness of deep sleep
when the elements and the rest
in the unreal, unmanifest, like nonbeing
when they have been dissolved by sleep
who then remains awake, free from ego
this is the construction with the third [verse]
ननु यदि तदा विनिद्रः असौ अस्ति
but if he is awake then
तर्हि जाग्रत्-स्वप्नयोः इव स्फुटः किम् न अवभासते
why does he not appear clearly, as in waking and dreaming?
he answers: previously he is the seer
clearly perceived as a seer, with distinctions
because the elements and the rest, which are objects of ego, have dissolved
when the ego relating to them has ceased
although the Self itself is not destroyed
one falsely thinks oneself to be destroyed
for one thing’s destruction appearing as another’s destruction, the example is
like a distressed and helpless person who has lost his wealth
the meaning is that he appears as if destroyed
but surely nothing is experienced in deep sleep
सुखम् अहम् अस्वाप्सम् न किञ्चिद् अवेदिषम्
इति विशेष-ज्ञानं विना केवलस्य आत्मनः प्रतिसन्धानात्
because the bare Self is recollected without particular cognition
but if recollection makes ego appear
how can there be absence of ego?
of the substance, the aggregate of cause and effect, endowed with ego
the support, the illuminator, and the abiding state
because ego too is seen as an attribute of a substance
the Self that sees it is distinct from it
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration:
idānīṃ suṣupti-sākṣitvena śuddhātma-pratipattim anubhavato darśayati tribhiḥ | bhūtādiṣv asaty asat-tulye’vyākṛte nidrayā līneṣu satsu yas tatra tadā vinidro nirahaṅkriyas tam ātmānaṃ pratipadyata iti tṛtīyenānvayaḥ ||14||

nanu yadi tadā vinidro’sāv asti tarhi jāgrat-svapnayor iva sphuṭaḥ kiṃ nāvabhāsate tatrāha---pūrvaṃ sa draṣṭāto draṣṭṛtvena sa-vikalpatayā sphuṭaṃ pratītaḥ | suṣuptau tu bhūtāder ahaṅkāra-viṣayasya līnatvāt tad viṣaye’haṅkāre naṣṭe sati svayam anaṣṭo’pi mṛṣaivātmānaṃ naṣṭavan manyamāno yaḥ | anyasya nāśe’nyasya naṣṭa-tulyatve dṛṣṭāntaḥ, naṣṭa-vitto yathā āturo vivaśaḥ, naṣṭavad bhavatīty arthaḥ ||15||

nanu suṣuptau na kiñcid anubhūyate, maivam, "sukham aham asvāpsaṃ na kiñcid avediṣam" iti viśeṣa-jñānaṃ vinā kevalasyātmanaḥ pratisandhānād ity āha---evam iti | nanu pratisandhāne sāhaṅkārasya pratīteḥ kathaṃ nirahaṅkriyatvaṃ tatrāha---sāhaṅkārasya dravyasya kārya-kāraṇa-saṅghātasyānugrahaḥ prakāśakaḥ avasthānaṃ ca | dravya-viśeṣaṇatayāhaṅkārasyāpi dṛśyatvāc ca tad draṣṭātmā tad vyatiriktaḥ | tam ātmānam ity anvayaḥ ||16||
entries.literal_english: Now Śrīdhara shows in three verses how the pure Self is realized as the witness of deep sleep. When the elements and the rest, unreal and unmanifest like non-being, have been dissolved by sleep, the one who remains awake and free from ego realizes that Self; this is the construction with the third verse. One may ask: if he is awake then, why does he not appear clearly as in waking or dreaming? Previously he is clearly perceived as a seer, with distinctions. In deep sleep, however, the objects of ego have dissolved; when ego related to them has ceased, the Self remains undestroyed, yet one falsely thinks oneself destroyed, like a distressed and helpless person who has lost his wealth. One may object that nothing is experienced in deep sleep. Not so: the recollection “I slept happily; I knew nothing” reconnects one with the bare Self without particular cognition. If this recollection makes ego appear, how can the Self be without ego? The aggregate of causes and effects endowed with ego is supported, illuminated, and maintained; since ego too is seen as an attribute of a substance, the witnessing Self is distinct from it. This is the construction with “that Self.”

entries.sanskrit: भक्ति-विरक्तिभ्यां सत्य् अपि विवेके प्रकृति-पुरुषयोः परस्पर-त्यागाभावात् कतहं मुक्तिर् इति पृच्छति, पुरुषम् इति चतुर्भिः । पुरुष-व्यतिरेकेण प्रकृतेः स्वरूप-लाभाभावात् प्रकृति-व्यतिरेकेण पुरुषस्याभिव्यक्त्य्-अभावाद् इत्य् अन्योन्यापाश्रयत्वान् नित्यत्वाच् च पुरुषं प्रकृतिः कदाचिन् न मुञ्चतीत्य् अर्थः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: even when discrimination exists through devotion and detachment
because Prakṛti and Puruṣa do not abandon one another
she asks, “How can there be liberation?”
[the Lord answers] in four verses beginning with “puruṣam”
because Prakṛti cannot obtain its own manifest form apart from Puruṣa
because Puruṣa is not manifested apart from Prakṛti
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: bhakti-viraktibhyāṃ saty api viveke prakṛti-puruṣayoḥ paraspara-tyāgābhāvāt katahaṃ muktir iti pṛcchati, puruṣam iti caturbhiḥ | puruṣa-vyatirekeṇa prakṛteḥ svarūpa-lābhābhāvāt prakṛti-vyatirekeṇa puruṣasyābhivyakty-abhāvād ity anyonyāpāśrayatvān nityatvāc ca puruṣaṃ prakṛtiḥ kadācin na muñcatīty arthaḥ ||17||
entries.literal_english: Even when discrimination exists through devotion and detachment, Devahūti asks how there can be liberation if Prakṛti and Puruṣa do not abandon one another. The Lord answers in four verses beginning “Puruṣam.” Prakṛti cannot obtain its own manifest form apart from Puruṣa, and Puruṣa is not manifested apart from Prakṛti. Because they depend on one another and are eternal, Prakṛti never releases Puruṣa; that is the meaning.

entries.sanskrit: व्यतिरेकाभाव-मात्रे दृष्टान्तः---यथा व्यतिरेकतो भावः सत्ता नास्ति । गन्धस्य कदाचिद् अपक्षय-दर्शनाद् दृष्टान्तान्तरम्---अपाम् इति । बुद्धेः प्रकृतेः । परस्य पुरुषस्य च ॥१८॥
word_for_word: an example for mere absence of separateness
as separate existence is not real
from the occasional observed loss of fragrance
entries.literal_english: For the mere absence of separateness, Śrīdhara gives an example: a thing has no real existence apart from its basis. Another example is the occasional observed loss of fragrance, introduced by “of the waters.” “Intellect” means Prakṛti, and “the Supreme” means Puruṣa.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: ततः किम् अत आह---अकर्तुर् इति । ये गुणा आश्रयो यस्य सः । तेषु प्रकृतेर् गुणेषु सत्सु पुरुषस्य कैवल्यं कथम् ? ॥१९॥
word_for_word: one for whom the guṇas are the support
when those guṇas of Prakṛti are present
how can there be isolation of Puruṣa?
entries.literal_english: Then what follows? Śrīdhara explains “of the non-agent”: [Puruṣa is] one whose support is the guṇas. When the guṇas of Prakṛti are present, how can Puruṣa be isolated?
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: tataḥ kim ata āha---akartur iti | ye guṇā āśrayo yasya saḥ | teṣu prakṛter guṇeṣu satsu puruṣasya kaivalyaṃ katham ? ||19||

entries.sanskrit: अत एव क्वचिन् निवृत्त-प्रायस्यापि संसार-भयस्य पुनर् उद्भवो दृश्यत इत्य् आह---क्वचिद् इति ॥२०॥
word_for_word: even when the fear of saṃsāra has almost ceased
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: ata eva kvacin nivṛtta-prāyasyāpi saṃsāra-bhayasya punar udbhavo dṛśyata ity āha---kvacid iti ||20||
entries.literal_english: For this very reason, the fear of saṃsāra is sometimes seen to arise again even after it has almost ceased, as Śrīdhara explains with “sometimes.”

entries.sanskrit: न हि प्रकृति-संबन्ध-मात्रं बन्ध-हेतुः, किन्तु गुण-बुद्ध्या तद्-आसक्तिस् तन्-निवृत्तौ सत्यां मोक्षो घटते । क्वचिद् उद्भवस् तु साधन-वैकल्याद् इत्य् अभिप्रेत्य साधनातिशयं कथयन् परिहरति त्रिभिः । निमित्तं फलम् । तन् न निमित्तं प्रवर्तकं यस्मिन्, तेन निष्कामेन धर्मेण । अमलात्मना निर्मलेन मनसा । श्रुतेन कथा-श्रवणेन संभृतया पुष्टया ॥२१॥ दह्यमाना अभिभूयमाना तिरो-हिता भवति ॥२३॥
word_for_word: mere connection with Prakṛti is not the cause of bondage
rather, it is attachment to it through taking the guṇas as the Self
but occasional recurrence is due to deficiency in the means
describing the excellence of the means
that [fruit] is not the motivating cause in which
by a stainless self, that is, by a pure mind
by hearing, by listening to the account
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: na hi prakṛti-saṃbandha-mātraṃ bandha-hetuḥ, kintu guṇa-buddhyā tad-āsaktis tan-nivṛttau satyāṃ mokṣo ghaṭate | kvacid udbhavas tu sādhana-vaikalyād ity abhipretya sādhanātiśayaṃ kathayan pariharati tribhiḥ | nimittaṃ phalam | tan na nimittaṃ pravartakaṃ yasmin, tena niṣkāmena dharmeṇa | amalātmanā nirmalena manasā | śrutena kathā-śravaṇena saṃbhṛtayā puṣṭayā ||21|| dahyamānā abhibhūyamānā tiro-hitā bhavati ||23||
entries.literal_english: Mere connection with Prakṛti is not the cause of bondage; rather, bondage is attachment to Prakṛti through identifying with the guṇas. When that attachment ceases, liberation occurs. Its occasional reappearance is due to deficiency in the means. With this in mind, Śrīdhara answers in three verses while describing the excellence of the means. “Nimitta” means fruit. Desireless duty is that in which the fruit is not the motivating cause. “With a stainless self” means with a pure mind. Devotion, strengthened by hearing the account, is nourished. When it is burned and overcome, it disappears.

entries.sanskrit: एवं च सति पुनर् उद्भवो नास्तीत्य् आह---भुक्तो भोगो यस्याः । नित्यशः सदा दृष्टो दोषो यस्याः । अत एव परित्यक्ता सतीश्वरस्यापरतन्त्रस्य स्वे महिम्नि स्थितस्य स्वानन्दं प्राप्तस्य ॥२४॥
word_for_word: who abides in His own majesty
who has attained His own bliss
entries.literal_english: When this is so, there is no reappearance. Śrīdhara explains: “she whose enjoyment is exhausted; whose fault is always seen.” Therefore Prakṛti is abandoned by the independent Lord, who abides in His own majesty and has attained His own bliss.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: अविवेकावस्थायाम् अनर्थ-हेतुर् अपि विवेकानन्तरं न भवतीति स-दृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति द्वाभ्याम् । प्रस्वापः स्वप्नः बह्व्-अनर्थान् बिभर्ति पुष्णाति । प्रतिबुद्धस्य संस्कार-वशेन स्फुरन्न् अपि ॥२५॥
word_for_word: it is not so after discrimination
it bears and nourishes many troubles
even though it appears to one awakened, by the force of impressions
entries.literal_english: Even what causes trouble in the state of non-discrimination does not do so after discernment; Śrīdhara gives an example in two verses beginning “as.” Deep sleep is a dream that bears and nourishes many troubles, even though it appears to one who has awakened through the force of impressions.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: न कतमेनापि व्याख्यातम् ।
entries.source_note: The pinned source explicitly says “न कतमेनापि व्याख्यातम् ।” (not explained by any commentator); this is no commentary, not a source gap.
entries.literal_english: No commentary by any commentator.

entries.sanskrit: उपसंहरति---यदैवम् इति त्रिभिः । बहूनि जन्मानि यस्मिन् काले ॥२७॥
word_for_word: at the time comprising many births
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara concludes in three verses beginning “When thus,” speaking of the time in which many births have occurred.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: प्रतिबुद्धार्थो विदितात्म-तत्त्वः । कैवल्याख्यं स्व-संस्थानं देहादि-व्यतिरिक्तं स्वरूपं मद्-आश्रयं निःश्रेयसं निरतिशयानन्दम् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: one who has awakened to the truth
one who has known the truth of the Self
one’s own nature, distinct from the body and the rest
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: pratibuddhārtho viditātma-tattvaḥ | kaivalyākhyaṃ sva-saṃsthānaṃ dehādi-vyatiriktaṃ svarūpaṃ mad-āśrayaṃ niḥśreyasaṃ niratiśayānandam ||28||
entries.literal_english: “One who has awakened to the truth” means one who has known the truth of the Self. The state called kaivalya is one’s own condition: a nature distinct from the body and the rest, resting in Me, the highest good, and unsurpassed bliss.

entries.sanskrit: स्व-दृशा आत्म-ज्ञानेन छिन्नाः संशया मिथ्या-ज्ञानानि यस्य लिङ्गाद् विनिर्गमे लिङ्ग-शरीर-नाशे सतीत्य् अर्थः ॥२९॥
word_for_word: by one’s own sight, that is, by knowledge of the Self
whose doubts and false cognitions have been cut off
upon departure from the liṅga [subtle body]
when the subtle body is destroyed
entries.literal_english: “By one’s own sight” means by knowledge of the Self. The person whose doubts and false cognitions have been cut off is so described upon departing from the liṅga [subtle body], that is, when the subtle body is destroyed.
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.

entries.sanskrit: तदा त्व् अणिमादि-सिद्धयोऽन्तराय-रूपा भवन्ति । तासु योगेनोपचितासु समृद्धासु न योगाद् अन्यो हेतुर् यासां, तासु यदा सिद्धस्य चेतो न विषज्जते । अङ्ग ! हे मातः ! अथ तदा अन्तम् अतिक्रान्तोऽत्यन्तो योऽहं, तत्-सम्बन्धिनी । यत्र यस्यां गतौ मृत्योर् हासो न भवति । विषक्टौ तु सिद्धोऽपि मया वशी-कृत इति मृत्योर् हासो गर्वो भवतीत्य् अर्थः ॥३०॥
word_for_word: when they have been augmented and developed through yoga
for which there is no cause other than yoga
तासु यदा सिद्धस्य चेतः न विषज्जते
when the mind of the perfected yogin is not attached to them
in that destination, in that state
Death has no occasion to laugh
“even a perfected one has been brought under my control”
Death’s laughter is pride; that is, it boasts
entries.source_note: Transcribed from Śrīdhara Svāmī’s Bhāvārtha-dīpikā block in the pinned source.
transliteration: tadā tv aṇimādi-siddhayo’ntarāya-rūpā bhavanti | tāsu yogenopacitāsu samṛddhāsu na yogād anyo hetur yāsāṃ, tāsu yadā siddhasya ceto na viṣajjate | aṅga ! he mātaḥ ! atha tadā antam atikrānto’tyanto yo’haṃ, tat-sambandhinī | yatra yasyāṃ gatau mṛtyor hāso na bhavati | viṣakṭau tu siddho’pi mayā vaśī-kṛta iti mṛtyor hāso garvo bhavatīty arthaḥ ||30||
entries.literal_english: At that point the powers beginning with aṇimā become obstacles. When they have been augmented and developed through yoga—having no cause other than yoga—and the mind of the perfected yogin is not attached to them, then, O dear mother, he reaches a state connected with Me, who transcend every limit. In that destination Death has no occasion to laugh. If attachment remains, however, Death laughs proudly, [thinking] “Even a perfected one has been brought under my control.”
